title: Continuous extension of the universal differential to a local completion
statement: Let $k$ be a commutative ring and $A$ a commutative local $k$-algebra with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$. Put $C=\widehat A$ as in [def-trf-formal-local-presentation], $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak mC$, and $M=C\otimes_A\Omega_{A/k}$ using [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]; this is the completed differential module of [def-trf-completed-jacobian-presentation]. A $k$-derivation $D:C\to M$ is a continuous extension of the universal differential if (i) $D(\iota(a))=1\otimes\mathrm da$ for every $a\in A$, where $\iota:A\to C$ is the completion map; and (ii) for every integer $r\ge0$ there exists an integer $N\ge0$ such that $D(x)\in\mathfrak n^rM$ for every $x\in\mathfrak n^N$. This is a predicate on the specified derivation, with no assertion of existence or uniqueness.
